summary: April CPI came in at 3.8% year over year, topping the 3.7% consensus, reinforcing a Fed hold and markets pricing in a near-98% chance of no rate change in June, while the odds of a hike by December have risen to nearly 30%. Simultaneously, trade and tariffs are a major focus this week as the U.S.-China summit gets underway, keeping bond yields elevated and squeezing gold's safe-haven premium against surging equities.
tweet: Hot April CPI cements a Fed hold through mid-year as a U.S.-China summit keeps tariff risk front and center, splitting stocks and bonds sharply.
